newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares drop on expectations of slow rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares drop on expectations of slow rate cuts.

text.p: Greek equities fell another 1.33 percent on Thursday on low volume said market watchers said the drop was due to expectations of interest rates declining at a slower pace in the future.

"The general share index dropped on Thursday because of market expectations of milder interest rate cuts. Wednesday's bond auction signalled that rates might have bottomed out for now," said analyst Nikos Kostopoulos at Commercial Securities.
But other brokers said they did not think the bonds' auction had an adverse effect on the bourse today.

"I do not think that the bourse's drop was a result of the auction. It is, rather, the outcome of a general bad sentiment in the market and the index's attempt to stabilise before rising to new highs," said broker Alexandros Devletoglou, of Devletoglou Securities.

The Athens general share index ended 1.33 percent or 17.11 points lower at 1,268.67 points from Wednesday's 1,285.78 after opening at 1283.25. Turnover was 8.1 billion drachmas on volume of 2.6 million shares.
